action: Passengers should wait for Thai Airways' individual notice and treat unexpected emails or calls about bookings with caution; the airline says it is investigating with Amadeus.
title: Thai Airways says supplier Amadeus reported unauthorised access to its booking data
date_note: Date of Thai Airways' own disclosure as stated in the article; the article was published 11 November.
exec: A booking-system supplier's incident exposed passenger booking data at an airline; supplier incidents can reach customers' data.
plain: Thai Airways says its booking-system supplier Amadeus reported that an unauthorised person accessed booking data. About 60,529 items were affected; the airline says its own systems were not involved.
summary: Thai Airways said on 10 November that Amadeus IT Group, its reservation-system provider, told it an unauthorised person accessed booking data stored in Amadeus's system. A preliminary check found about 60,529 items with names, booking references, travel dates, routes and cabin class; about 376 more may hold extra details such as contact and passport data. The airline says the incident was not in its own system and front-side credit card data was unaffected.

validation.note: Single publisher (Naewna) relaying Thai Airways' statement; the airline's own notice and Amadeus's statement were not read. The article does not say whether the 60,529 and 376 counts overlap.
